body: Lisa Su became CEO Oct 2014 with AMD near insolvency: ~$2.5bn debt, market cap <$2bn, stock just over $3 on her first day, falling to ~$1.61 (2015-16 low). Plan: exit low-margin businesses, bet the company on one high-performance core (Zen), use console semi-custom chips (PS4/Xbox One) for cash. Zen/Ryzen launched 2017 (+52% IPC claimed); EPYC servers 2017; Zen 3 (2020) took the single-thread lead from Intel. Two external helps: TSMC process (GlobalFoundries quit 7nm 2018) and Intel's 10nm delays. Stock tripled by mid-2016, crossed $100 in 2020, peaked ~$227 (Mar 2024) and ~$260s (Oct 2025 after the OpenAI GPU deal) [2025 peak unverified]; ~140x+ from trough. Split: started loss-making, so the move was earnings creation (EPS from negative to ~$3+ adj) plus P/S from ~0.3x to ~8-10x; classic loss-to-profit turnaround. Drawdowns: ~-67% Nov 2021-Oct 2022; also >-50% in 2018 [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2016: Zen engineering samples matching Intel Broadwell-E in public demos (Dec 2016); debt restructured; gross margin inching up from ~23% to 30%+ [unverified]; insider-led focus. Who caught it: mostly retail and tech growth funds; no single famous value investor documented. Status: market value ~$675-800bn cited 2026; GPU challenge to Nvidia ongoing. LESSON: an engineer-CEO with a single product bet, an outsourced manufacturing edge and a stumbling incumbent can create a 100x from near-bankruptcy; the first proof was a benchmark, not a quarterly EPS.

data.early_signals: Zen demos 2016, console cash, debt restructuring, Intel 10nm delays
data.lesson: engineer-CEO + one product bet + incumbent stumble

title: AMD 2014-2025: Lisa Su turnaround, ~$1.6 -> ~$200+
